claims.text: About 20–50% of Graves patients stay in remission after a 1–2 yr course of methimazole or PTU.
claims.quote: Approximately 20 to 50% of patients with Graves disease remain in remission after a 1- to 2-year course of either methimazole or propylthiouracil

claims.text: Methimazole: usual start 5–20 mg PO 1–3 times a day;
claims.quote: The usual starting dose of methimazole is 5 to 20 mg orally 1 to 3 times a day.

claims.text: once T4/T3 normalize, lower to the lowest effective dose, usually 2.5–10 mg once a day, to avoid hypothyroidism.
claims.quote: when T4 and T3 levels normalize, the dosage is decreased to the lowest effective amount, usually methimazole 2.5 to 10 mg once a day in order to avoid inducing hypothyroidism.
Control generally is achieved in 2 to 3 months.
Methimazole is contraindicated in the presence of hypersensitivity to the drug or any of the other product components.

claims.text: Methimazole crosses the placenta and can cause fetal harm in the first trimester.
claims.quote: Methimazole crosses the placental membranes and can cause fetal harm, when administered in the first trimester of pregnancy.

claims.text: Warfarin effect may increase (consider more PT/INR checks).
claims.quote: the activity of oral anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) may be increased; additional monitoring of PT/INR should be considered

claims.text: Once euthyroid: beta-blocker dose may need lowering;
claims.quote: A dose reduction of beta-adrenergic blockers may be needed when a hyperthyroid patient becomes euthyroid.

claims.text: digoxin levels may rise, so its dose may need lowering;
claims.quote: Serum digitalis levels may be increased when hyperthyroid patients on a stable digitalis glycoside regimen become euthyroid; a reduced dosage of digitalis glycosides may be needed.

claims.text: theophylline clearance may fall, so its dose may need lowering.
claims.quote: Theophylline clearance may decrease when hyperthyroid patients on a stable theophylline regimen become euthyroid; a reduced dose of theophylline may be needed.

claims.text: Contact the prescriber right away if pregnant or planning pregnancy.
claims.quote: Patients should be advised that if they become pregnant or intend to become pregnant while taking an antithyroid drug, they should contact their physician immediately about their therapy.

claims.text: Agranulocytosis is less common with methimazole <20 mg/day; with PTU it may occur at any dose.
claims.quote: when methimazole is used in dosages of < 20 mg a day, agranulocytosis is less common; with propylthiouracil, agranulocytosis may occur at any dosage.

claims.text: If it occurs with one, don't switch to the other; use RAI or surgery.
claims.quote: If agranulocytosis occurs with one of the antithyroid peroxidase medications (methimazole or propylthiouracil), avoid using another medication in the same class; use another therapy (eg, radioiodine, surgery) instead.
